mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based contraction in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) both rise together by more than 0.5% in the same month, it signals a stagflation risk, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.5% AND CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 50,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which initially boosts consumer spending but eventually leads to higher wage growth and input costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in an expansionary regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 50,000 for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes during expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for three consecutive months, regardless of GDP trend, signals weakening consumer demand and presages negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
